page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable x86_64 virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, the instance features 1 physical core configured with hyper-threading to provide 2 vCPUs. Hardware resource allocation includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, with L3 cache measuring 35 MB. Supported instruction sets encompass AVX, AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and FMA. This instance type includes no local NVMe storage and zero baseline dedicated network bandwidth.

Synthetic benchmarks highlight modest performance characteristics consistent with burstable CPU limits. Multi-core performance registered a stress-ng score of 2402.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1850. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 20.68 GB/sec, while write operations measured 16.39 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show static web serving throughput at 2.44 GB/sec and Redis SET performance at 2.57 million operations per second. For small 135M parameter LLM inference, prompt processing achieved 97.08 tokens per second and text generation reached 21.85 tokens per second.

By employing a burstable CPU allocation model, ecs.t6-c1m2.large offers low baseline compute costs for applications with intermittent operational spikes. However, sustained heavy compute loads will deplete CPU credits and reduce performance output. The instance is suited for lightweight workloads such as low-traffic web servers, development environments, background workers, microservices, and small utility tasks where continuous CPU utilization is not required.
